chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Early radio broadcasts of Kid Ory on KFI
summary: Spikes took Ory's band to KFI in the Packard Building in 1921, the first Black band on radio there; Mosby later broadcast from the Alabam.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Uh, were there...did you ever play over the radio here? It said Kid Ory played over KFI. Was that when he worked in your club?
Yeah. Yeah. We used to let him go down there and play.
You had a...oh, he went to the radio station. They didn't have like a radio broadcast out of a club?

Yeah. No. Mosby was the first one I think had that. Mosby, when he had the Alabam, I think he had broadcastin' right from there. You know, he had...you could rent the machine, and they'd come down and put it in, and...but...I was one that put Kid Ory 'n' them on there afore any of them had 'em. That was the first Negro band... I used to have to carry 'em to the station which was on, I think, Twelfth and Olive...or Twelfth and Hope or somewhere. It was in the old Packard Building where they sold Packard cars, and it was KFI.
Is that the same station that Mosby had at the Alabam?
I don't remember what...I know he...I think he had one in there but I don't know what station his was.
